title: f82r.12 as attachment followed by a rigid-body consequence
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Read the complete otedy ... okal line as fastening an A component to the upper face of B and then turning B over. Fastening versus mere placement predicts whether the same A must turn with B and preserve its relative pose. Both whole labels are already documented; no physical component owner or action word is confirmed.

finite_provisional_grammar.argument_rule: The Object before FASTEN is A; the Object inside OF is B. Completing the fastening clause sets the current target to B. A following argumentless TURNOVER acts on that target. No new target is guessed at the second action.
finite_provisional_grammar.scope_rule: Clauses follow written order. Juxtaposition is the declared clause sequencer; no extra written conjunction is claimed. The face is body-relative to B at fastening time, not permanently the page upper side.
finite_provisional_grammar.whole_text_debt: Only this complete line has a proposed parse. The surrounding paragraph and all other occurrences require the same class, argument and word rules; they are not silently neutral. No special line-ID rule licenses this syntax.

exact_semantic_model.state: A finite set of rigid planar bodies with poses and an attachment graph. Local body/face owners must be supplied by the proposed reading, not by arbitrary object IDs.
exact_semantic_model.fasten: Require distinct bodies A and B and a specified upper face of B; place A there and add a rigid attachment preserving their relative transform.
exact_semantic_model.turnover: Rotate current target B by 180 degrees about its declared anchor and apply the same rigid transform to every body rigidly connected to B.
exact_semantic_model.consequence: The relative transform inverse(pose(B))*pose(A) stays unchanged. A moves with B; a subsequent instruction treating A as detached would require an explicit release.
exact_semantic_model.written_order_consequence: Fasten A then turn B rotates A. Turn B first and only then fasten A on its upper body-relative face does not entail the same final absolute pose of A. The two instructions do not generally commute.

explicit_rival.only_changed_word: qodched = place, creating no rigid edge

explicit_rival.different_consequence: A is not forced by a rigid constraint to follow B. Relative-pose preservation is no longer entailed. A mere inventory or static adjacency description entails neither operation.
explicit_rival.limit: No observed A trajectory, before/after diagram or definite face owner is currently bound. This is a prospective semantic discriminator, not a measured success.

novelty_and_predecessors: P28 primary leaves the complete eight-word relation open and shows that otedy and okal must be jointly available under its name hypothesis. This card makes a concrete complete relation proposal instead of another namespace switch.

S12 primary gives directed joins on f21r/f29v but no bound later component treatment and no selected assembly interpretation. Here a distinct written final group is prospectively assigned an operation whose result depends on attachment. That assignment is a new hypothesis, not evidence that the old missing continuation was solved.
GDT221 and GDT222 primaries retain failed/coverage-unstable label-to-assembly transfer. This card does not infer a component owner from their modules or scores.

GDT792 primary establishes cross-scope whole-form reuse for okal, not an address, named object or material. P28 retains ambiguous L14 ownership and no proved shared cross-page apparatus. These objections remain.
design.strongest_objection: The proposed fastening and turn are supplied by six new unconfirmed function/content values, while the images may depict bodies or an entirely different kind of object. Label reuse alone does not establish two rigid components, their faces, the half-turn, or the continuation grammar. Without independently constrained poses or other complete uses, any apparent coherence would just be a constructed mechanical story.
design.prospective_review: Retain RAW. Before selection, require the same finite clause grammar to explain all selected whole occurrences and a complete paragraph; seek an already admitted owner/consequence capable of distinguishing attachment from placement. Missing physical owners must remain missing. Do not choose new component IDs, rotations or an attachment law after viewing a favorable outcome.
